horizon_driver: national electoral cycle (next general election 2029) plus state-election calendar that periodically forces short-term populist spending/energy-price decisions

constraints.source: post-independence non-alignment doctrine, now rebranded 'strategic autonomy'; never entered a binding mutual-defense treaty
constraints.breaks_under: not observed to break even under sustained China border pressure (2020 Galwan) or intense US courtship

constraints.source: energy security and refining-margin arbitrage (discounted Urals crude), domestic fuel-price political sensitivity
constraints.breaks_under: already partially broken downward under US tariff pressure: imports fell from ~1.71mbd average in 2025 to ~1.16mbd in Feb 2026 after the 25% additional US tariff, then stabilized around 0.8-1.0mbd after a Feb 2026 US-India trade deal and a Supreme Court ruling constraining US tariff authority

constraints.source: decades of platform interoperability, spare-parts dependency, and pricing advantage
constraints.breaks_under: diversifying, not abandoning: France now ~28-29% of 2021-25 arms imports vs Russia's ~40% (down from historic highs), yet India approved ~$25bn in new purchases including 5 additional S-400 systems as recently as March 2026

stated_vs_revealed.stated: India buys Russian oil purely on economic/energy-security grounds, apolitically, and rejects any external 'permission' requirement (March 2026 government statement).
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Import volumes tracked US political pressure almost exactly: cut roughly in half (1.71mbd to 1.16mbd) after the Aug 2025 25% additional tariff, then partially recovered once the tariff was rolled back in the Feb 2026 interim trade deal and a Supreme Court IEEPA ruling constrained Trump's tariff authority. The 'apolitical energy security' framing is itself a negotiating posture.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Confirms the classic madhyama pattern: India extracts maximum flexibility by publicly denying that its energy policy is a bargaining chip while privately calibrating it precisely to external leverage.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: India is diversifying away from Russian defense dependence toward Western suppliers (France, Israel, US) as strategic policy.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Diversification is real (France ~28-29% share 2021-25 vs Russia ~40%, down from Cold-War-era near-monopoly) but not a substitution: India approved a fresh ~$25bn package in March 2026 including five additional S-400 batteries, alongside continuing T-90S and Su-30 upgrades from Russia.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: 'Diversification' in Indian usage means adding suppliers, not replacing Russia — the two tracks run in parallel rather than one displacing the other.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: The Feb 2026 US-India trade deal and Quad participation signal India consolidating as 'a primary US ally and critical counterweight to China'.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Simultaneously, India is hosting/co-launching BRICS Pay (a SWIFT/dollar-alternative settlement rail integrating UPI, CIPS, SPFS and Pix) at the Sept 12-13 2026 New Delhi BRICS summit, and continues large-scale Russian energy and defense purchases — hedging both the US-aligned and BRICS/multipolar tracks at once.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: India accepts a preferential US tariff (18%, lower than Vietnam/Bangladesh) while simultaneously deepening the institutional plumbing of a dollar-alternative bloc; both postures are being monetized concurrently, not sequentially.

tripwires.if: the US Congress passes and enforces the proposed up-to-100% secondary tariff bill targeting top-5 Russian oil/gas importers
tripwires.then: India cuts Russian crude imports further toward the 500-800kbd range rather than accept a blanket 100% tariff, prioritizing the larger US export market over the Russian discount

tripwires.if: a major India-China LAC border incident occurs
tripwires.then: India accelerates Quad defense cooperation and Western procurement visibly within one quarter, despite continuing to deny any formal alliance shift

tripwires.if: Hormuz or Gulf shipping is disrupted and Brent spikes above ~$100
tripwires.then: India increases discounted Russian barrel purchases regardless of Western political pressure, since energy-security/current-account math dominates alignment signaling at that point

what_would_change_my_mind: A sustained (2+ quarter) cut of Russian oil imports below 500kbd absent a further tariff shock, or India signing a binding mutual-defense-style clause with the US/Quad, would indicate the hedging strategy is being abandoned rather than optimized — that would be the signal a side-choice is being forced rather than resisted.
